advaita-prakasha.title: Рождение близнецов Сварупы и Джагадиши (джьештха 1430 г. Шака)
advaita-prakasha.summary: В месяце джьештха 1430 г. Шака у Ситы рождаются близнецы, которых нарекают Сварупой и Джагадишей; астролог предсказывает им мирскую учёность и любовь друг к другу, как у Лавы и Куши.

verses.text: Затем, в месяце Джьештха 1430 года эры Шака, у Ситы родились сыновья-близнецы.
В должное время совершили наречение двух младенцев и, выбрав, дали им имена Сварупа и Джагадиша.
Астролог сказал: «Оба будут умны и в мирской учёности сравнятся с царями.
Между ними будет любовь, как у Лавы и Куши, и голоса у них будут нежны, как у гандхарвов».
Затем в должное время, с радостью дав маха-прасад, совершили первое кормление обоих.
Множество брахманов и вайшнавов радостно отобедали и, получив одежды и каури, все благословили детей.

verses_en.text: Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Sitanatha! Glory to Nityananda-Rama together with the devotees!
Now I shall tell of other chief branches of the Lord: earlier I did not write of them, so as not to break the order.
In the month of Pausha in the year 1426 of the Shaka era, the fourth son of Sita appeared.
Some said that Indra had come down and been born, others that the moon had appeared.
In due time the priest-astrologer came and, having calculated, told the truth about the newborn.
The brahmana said: "This child is the incarnation of Kubera: the mercy of Kamala (Lakshmi) upon him is great.
In intellect he will equal Brihaspati; he will be learned and exceedingly handsome,
but he will lodge false reasoning in the true dharma; in the end, in the company of saints, that error will go."
Hearing this, the Vaishnavas cried out the name of Hari, and the women with joy in their hearts made the "ulu-ulu" sound.
(The priest) said: "This boy will be strong; therefore I name him Balarama."
When Sriman Balarama was seven months old, Sitanatha performed his first rice-feeding.
On this occasion He offered food to Krishna, held a festival and fed the blind, the poor, the brahmanas and the Vaishnavas.
Presenting everyone with clothes and cowries, He honoured them, and all, giving their blessings, went to their homes.
Then, in the month of Jyeshtha in the year 1430 of the Shaka era, twin sons were born to Sita.
In due time the naming of the two infants was performed, and, choosing, they gave them the names Svarupa and Jagadisha.
The astrologer said: "Both will be intelligent and in worldly learning will equal kings.
There will be love between them like that of Lava and Kusha, and their voices will be as sweet as those of Gandharvas."
Then in due time, joyfully giving maha-prasada, the first rice-feeding of both was performed.
Many brahmanas and Vaishnavas dined joyfully and, receiving clothes and cowries, all blessed the children.
One day the Lord, having finished the evening arati to Krishna, was loudly singing the name of Hari with the devotees.
At that time a Vaishnava came there and told the Lord the news from Nadia.
The Vaishnava said: "Nimai has left home: He came to the town of Katwa and shaved His head.
Keshava Bharati initiated Him into sannyasa and gave Him the name Sri Krishna Chaitanya.
In her grief for Him Mother Shachi has no external awareness: she falls senseless wherever she is.
Now, crying 'Ah, Nimai!', she weeps aloud — at that grief stones split as if struck by lightning.
Now, like one distraught, she rushes hither and thither; now she goes to the bank of the Ganga to die.
Of Mother Vishnupriya one cannot even speak: the clouds of her ceaseless tears flood the world."
Hearing this, the Lord was stunned, and after a watch He wept aloud.
Learning the reason, Sita wept loudly, and Advaita's companions floated in an ocean of grief.
In the second watch the Lord laughed loudly — who has the power to understand even a shadow of it?
In the ecstasy of love for Gaura that night passed. Then the Lord said to His intimate devotees:
"The shore of the great ocean can in time be found, but the ocean of Krishna's mercy never has a shore.
To fulfil the desire of His devotees, how much humility He shows!
Krishna is eternally subject to His devotees — so say all the shastras; by this pastime He has given full proof of it."
As He spoke, He was overcome with love and said: "I have understood all Your tricks:
as an actor, putting on various costumes, captivates people, so You, to teach the people, have taken the guise of a sannyasi."
Then Advaitachandra's external awareness returned, and He loudly began the sankirtana of the Name.
At that time the venerable Sri Acharyaratna came to the house of Sitanatha.
Seeing him, the Lord asked anxiously: "Tell Me, tell Me quickly, what news from Nadia?"
Sri Acharyaratna replied: "Listen, Gosani: having accepted sannyasa, Nimai has come here."
Starting, the Lord asked: "Where is He?" Acharyaratna replied: "He has appeared on the other bank of the Ganga.
Take a boat, go and bring Him across: in the ecstasy of love He has been fasting for four days."
Hearing this, my Lord cried out in sorrow and hastily crossed the Ganga in a boat.
Gaura, overwhelmed with love, seeing Advaita's companions, said: "What a wonder — the Acharya has come to Vrindavana!"
Hearing this, the Lord said: "Wherever You appear, that is holy Vraja-dhama, say all the shastras."
Having said this, He took Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda with Him and, crossing the Ganga, set out for Shantipura.
Seeing Gauranga in the dress of a sannyasi, Mother Sita grieved so much that there was no measure to it.
Then Mother cooked much rice and many dishes, made cakes and everything that Gauranga loved.
Fragrant preparations cooked in ghee, full of divine nectar, Mother cooked in abundance with deep devotion.
Placing tulasi blossoms on top, she offered the food to Krishna with joy in her heart.
Then, inviting Gaura and Nityananda, she carefully seated them on divine seats.
At the Acharya's insistence both sat down to eat, while the Lord Himself stood to serve.
Seeing this, Gaura laughed and said to Sitanatha: "Without Shiva no sacrifice is ever successful."
Laughing, my Lord replied: "You are Shiva embodied: by Your mercy all souls obtain auspiciousness (shivatva)."
Mahaprabhu said: "Give up your tricks. Without you I can eat nothing."
Hearing this, Nityananda laughed loudly and said: "Listen to one word of Mine, merciful Gaura:
do not honour this glutton of a little brahmana: even if he eats with four hands, his belly will not be filled.
Sometimes he eats with his head, like fire; in such a great science he has no equal."
Hearing this, Sri Advaita said, laughing in loving anger: "It is You who, taking many forms, eat in every land.
You alone eat with countless mouths — who has the power to fill Your belly?"
Thus each revealed the truth about the other, and, listening, Gaura laughed softly.
Then Mahaprabhu, acting as arbiter, said: "Let us weigh you both on the scales — by your eating."
Hearing this, my Lord said in pure devotion: "You alone in the world have no measure:
in You is the measure of the infinite worlds; no other scales, it seems, are needed here."
Thus Mahaprabhu and the two Prabhus revealed the true essence by hints.
After the meal the three Thakuras rested and loudly proclaimed the great power of the company of saints.
Raising their arms, they said: "Listen, all! Inconceivable is the natural virtue of the company of saints.
A saint considers himself lower than a blade of grass; in tolerance he surpasses a tree;
in his mind there is no desire for honour, and he is always engaged in honouring others;
he ceaselessly sings the name of Hari — such are the true marks of a sadhu.
Take refuge, all of you, at the feet of the sadhus — thus you will obtain the true, eternal treasure, the goal of all endeavour.
Who can grasp the essence of the endless shastras? He who is wise mounts the chariot of the sadhus' path.
The sadhus, taking the essence of all the shastras, reveal the easy, true path.
Whoever walks that path has eyes; whoever turns away from it is like the blind.
As only a diamond can cut glass, but through a hole already made even a thread can pass,
so whoever walks the path laid by the sadhus, even if ignorant, crosses the ocean of existence.
Therefore the ancient rishis say: without the company of saints the heart does not become pure.
A sadhu by nature is equally merciful to all beings: by mere association he imparts his own nature to the soul.
As other insects, by association with the kumira insect, of themselves become like it,
so without the company of saints the path of worship is not determined, and righteous conduct and devotion to Krishna do not arise.
Even if someone is a great sinner and a villain — when the sun of a sadhu rises, he is surely purified.
As iron becomes gold at the touch of the philosopher's stone, so by the company of saints the soul becomes eternally free."
Thus they set forth hundreds of truths of the true dharma, and listening, the Sri Vaishnavas were immersed in bliss.
Meanwhile in Navadvipa Mahaprabhu's mother heard from people that Gaura had come to Shantipura.
Gathering with Gaura's devotees from Nadia, she joyfully arrived in Shantipura.
Seeing His mother, Sri Chaitanya prostrated Himself before her, and Shachi, looking at her son's face, began to weep.
Shachi said: "Nimai, seeing this appearance of yours, my heart splits as if struck by a rock."
The waves of the ocean of the mother's grief rose ever higher, and all the souls were carried away in that stream.
Mahaprabhu gave everyone a great teaching, and, hearing it, they were freed from all grief.
Then Shachi cooked fragrant shali rice and various dishes in ghee, dear to Gaura.
Sweet rice and other sweets surpassing nectar Sri Chaitanya joyfully tasted with His companions.
What bliss reigned for several days in the house of Sitanatha — who can describe it?
By day Mahaprabhu instructed in the Name, and at night He sang sankirtana with His associates and devotees.
Intoxicated with the bliss of love, Gaura's companions sprinkled Shantipura with tears of love.
One day Sri Gauranga very sweetly asked everyone's leave to go.
Hearing this, all the devotees were poisoned with the venom of grief, and in its burning all the souls tossed about.
What more can I say of the fire of Shachi's grief? If fire itself came near, it too would be burnt to ashes.
With cries of anguish Mother said to Gorachand: "Where will you go, leaving me in the snare of grief?
Do not go to Nadia — there is no harm in that: worship Hari, settling in this land."
Mahaprabhu replied: "Mother, do not say that: for a sannyasi to live in his homeland is against dharma."
Although Sri Shachi is a mine of maternal love, she, overcoming insurmountable ignorance, gave her son a command:
Mother said: "Vrindavana is a distant land. Live near Sri Purushottama — I shall receive news of you."
Placing His mother's command on His head, Sri Gauranga set out; His dear devotees fell at His feet.
The devotees said: "Shall we see You again or not? Let us gaze at You enough for a lifetime and comfort our hearts."
Hearing this, Sri Chaitanya, softened by compassion, said: "Do not grieve for Me.
Not only this time — birth after birth I am not parted from you for a moment.
As in this life you have celebrated with Me, so you will celebrate in two more lives.
Mine is only an empty body; you are the five breaths of My life: where shall I go, leaving you all, with an empty body?
Now, to keep the dharma of a sannyasi, I wander through various lands, holy places and sacred sites.
Gather together and sing the sankirtana of the Name every day, preach dharma and serve the sadhus.
Thus you will surely obtain the bliss of love. Do not despair on My account."
Thus Gora consoled all the devotees and, overwhelmed with love, set out for Sri Purushottama.
With Him went Nityananda, Sri Mukunda, Damodara Pandita and Sri Jagadananda.
On the way Sri Chaitanya by His mercy delivered many fallen people, unbelievers and evil-doers.
The four companions loudly sang the Name, while Gaura, in the ecstasy of love, went on roaring like a lion.
Continuing on, they came to holy Remuna and, seeing Gopinatha, all were filled with great bliss.
Gauranga, intoxicated with love, danced: now He wept, now ran, losing all sense of direction.
The flood of Lord Nityananda's love surged up: drawing in all the souls, it engulfed them.
Then, having seen Sakshi-Gopala, Gaurachandra arrived at Sri Purushottama.
Seeing Jagannatha, He was filled with mahabhava and, as if intoxicated, now wept, now laughed.
Then Gora fainted in the ecstasy of love; after a long time His external awareness returned a little.
There lived the most learned Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya, the crown of pandits, like Brihaspati.
Seeing the divine mahabhava in Gaura's body, he said: "This person must be a Great Personality."
Then he took Sri Gauranga to his own house, and Nityananda and the others came there.
Surrounding Gaura, all sang the sankirtana of the Name, and Gora, crying "Hari!", rose and began to dance.
Then the Bhatta had the Sri maha-prasada brought and carefully fed Chaitanya and His companions.
After some days Gaura revealed His divine glory, and seeing it, the Bhatta was filled with the jubilation of devotion.
Formerly Sarvabhauma held to dry knowledge; by the power of the philosopher's stone, Gaura, he became the best of devotees.
Then Gaura went round the holy places of the south and there met Raya Ramananda.
Raya was highly skilled in the correct conclusions of the scriptures of devotion; my Lord calls him an associate of Krishna.
There Ramananda spoke and Sri Chaitanya listened: superhuman moods that intoxicate the minds of the devotees.
Then Gaura returned again to Sri Purushottama and, seeing Jagannatha, was immersed in pure love.
He showed mercy to King Prataparudra through the devotees: to fulfil the desire of the devotees He displayed His majesty.
Gora, boundlessly merciful, became six-armed; beholding that form, the devotees were lost in love.
Some by good fortune drank that Ganga of the nectar of mercy, while others, not receiving it, lamented bitterly.
Bhagavan Himself is the embodiment of the nectar of mercy: surely His mercy is revealed through the devotees.
Then, on the occasion of Jagannatha's chariot festival, the Lord set out for Sri Kshetra to see Gauranga.
With the Acharya went countless devotees; Krishna Mishra too wished to go with them.
Sri Advaita said: "The road is very hard; there is no need for you to go now."
Krishna Mishra replied: "The world is without substance; the essence of truth is shelter at the feet of Sri Gauranga."
Although Krishna Mishra was always detached, by meditating on Gauranga his detachment became excessive.
Knowing this, Mother Sita said to Krishnadasa: "The time has not yet come for you to go to Sri Kshetra.
Listen, Krishna Mishra, place your mother's word on your head: stay at home, worship Krishna and do all that is good.
Your elder brother Achyuta has been detached from his youth; for the service of Krishna and of your father I consider you worthy.
Receive the mantra together with your wife Sri Vijaya: in the service of Krishna lies every perfection, there is no doubt."
Having said this, she took them both to the bank of the Ganga and gave them her own perfect mantra.
Having received the eternally perfect mantra of Krishna, the couple in the bliss of love bowed at their mother's feet and offered her praise.
I have told this secret event briefly. Then Sri Advaita set out for Sri Kshetra.
Meeting His own, Gaura was filled with great bliss and went round the town in a great sankirtana.
In front, with honour, they placed the Acharya; in the middle Gaura and Nityananda; behind came the devotees.
There was a wondrous dance that amazed the people; the minds of all were immersed in the sweetness of the kirtana.
By the nature of love some laughed, others wept, others thundered like clouds: "Hare Krishna!"
After a long time, ending the sankirtana of Hari, Mahaprabhu went to bathe with the devotees.
The merriment of Sri Advaita and Nityananda grew, and with the pure devotees they began to play in the water.
In the ecstasy of love Gora laid Advaita down, and my Lord, lying on the water, began to float.
In some rapture Gaura climbed onto His chest, and the Lord floated lovingly, carrying Mahaprabhu.
What power He showed — there is no limit to it; seeing it, the devotees were lost in the bliss of love.
As Maha-Vishnu lies on the bed of Ananta, so began Gaura's pastime on the bed of Advaita's body.
Seeing the wondrous display of the human pastimes of the two, all the devotees cried: "Hari! Hari!"
Thus, having displayed the pastime of the One who lies on Shesha, Gaura with His companions went to the Acharya's invitation.
Krishna Chaitanya dined with His own, and Sitanatha in the ecstasy of love offered praises.
This wondrous pastime I did not see: only one who is most fortunate saw it with his own eyes.
This nectar of rasa, flowing from the lotus lips of Shripada Nityananda Prabhu, I have drunk and been purified.
There is no counting the pastimes of Chaitanya and Advaita: I have written only a particle of their essence.
Placing his hope in the feet of Sri Chaitanya and Sri Advaita, Ishana Nagara tells the Advaita-prakasha.

bhakti-ratnakara.title: Санатана получает «Бхагавату» во сне и наяву
bhakti-ratnakara.summary: В ранней юности Санатане во сне брахман даёт «Шримад-Бхагавату», а утром тот же брахман вручает её наяву; Санатана погружается в прему и позже раскрывает смысл в «Вайшнава-тошани» (шлоки из «Лагху-тошани» Дживы).

verses.text:
Жизнь Шри Санатаны поистине удивительна;
он безмерно любит «Шримад-Бхагавату».

В ранней юности во сне некий почтенный брахман
с радостью в сердце даёт ему «Шримад-Бхагавату».

Проснувшись, Санатана пришёл в волнение —
[а наяву] тот самый брахман с любовью вручил ему «Шримад-Бхагавату».

Получив «Шри Бхагавату», с великой радостью в душе
господин мой погрузился в океан нектара премы.

Как он вкушал смысл «Шримад-Бхагаваты»,
он явил в «Шри Вайшнава-тошани».

О прошлом Шри Санатаны я скажу кратко;
Шри Джива Госвами подробно изложил его в «Тошани».

Так [сказано] в «Лагху-тошани»:
«Те, кто в ранней юности получил „Шри Бхагавату“ во сне, а утром, проснувшись, — от того самого брахмана, которого видели во сне,
и погрузился в великий океан нектара премы к Бхагавану, — это писание поистине их, тех, кого зовут Шри Санатана.
Поднеся его, Джива, чья жизнь — их стопы, желая сказать ещё кое-что, теперь подносит вот это»*.
notes: «Лагху-тошани» — сокращённая Дживой Госвами «Вайшнава-тошани» Санатаны (комментарий к 10-й песни «Бхагаваты»). Шлоки 537–539 и далее 569–577 (родословная) — из неё.

verses_en.text:
The life of Sri Sanatana is truly wondrous;
he loves the Srimad Bhagavatam beyond measure.

In his early youth, in a dream, a venerable brahmana
with joy in his heart gives him the Srimad Bhagavatam.

On waking, Sanatana was agitated —
[and in waking life] that same brahmana lovingly handed him the Srimad Bhagavatam.

Having received the Sri Bhagavata, with great joy at heart
my master sank into the ocean of the nectar of prema.

How he relished the meaning of the Srimad Bhagavatam
he revealed in the Sri Vaishnava-toshani.

Of Sri Sanatana's past I shall speak briefly;
Sri Jiva Gosvami set it out in detail in the Toshani.

Thus [it is said] in the Laghu-toshani:
"Those who in early youth received the Sri Bhagavata in a dream, and in the morning, awake, from the very brahmana they had seen in the dream,
and sank into the great ocean of the nectar of prema for Bhagavan — this writing is truly theirs, of those called Sri Sanatana.
Having offered it, Jiva, whose life is their feet, wishing to say something more, now offers this."*
notes: The Laghu-toshani is Jiva Gosvami's abridgement of Sanatana's Vaishnava-toshani (a commentary on the tenth canto of the Bhagavata). Verses 537–539 and further 569–577 (the genealogy) are from it.
